name: Conduct — Network Operations Governance
description: Hook-surface rules for governing autonomous NetOps agents. Blocks writes to security-sensitive network configuration (ACL, firewall, routing policy) while allowing reversible operational actions (QoS, service restart, logging). Companion pack for the network_diagnosis_agent playbook.

ui.subtitle: Hook-surface rule blocking autonomous writes to ACL / firewall / routing policy. Companion pack for the network_diagnosis_agent playbook.

rules.description: Block agent shell commands that modify security-sensitive network configuration (ACL, firewall, routing policy, RADIUS/AAA). Reversible operational actions (QoS, service restart, logging) remain allowed. Policy changes must go through human approval per the Level-5 autonomy tier.
rules.message: Blocked: this shell action would modify a security-sensitive network policy. Autonomous agents can propose the change and log the recommendation, but the commit must be approved by a human (Level 5 in the autonomy hierarchy).

enforcement.guarantee: Blocks the matching action only on hook and MCP surfaces when their listed dependencies are satisfied. Does NOT inspect LLM prompt or response text.
requires: A supported pre-tool hook is installed, synced, and invoked before the action
The agent invokes MCP guard_check with accurate tool_name and tool_input before acting
Conduct workflow runtime Guard is enabled and matching content is present in workflow state
known_limitations: Hook enforcement depends on the AI tool emitting supported structured hook events
MCP cannot enforce actions the agent does not submit to guard_check
Runtime evaluates serialized workflow state, not every external tool or model interaction

rules.description: Block agent shell / API actions that mutate RADIUS / AAA / ClearPass identity policy — service enforcement, role mapping, authentication method changes. Autonomous agents can propose the change and log the recommendation, but the commit must be approved by a human (Level 5 autonomy).
rules.message: Blocked: this action would modify RADIUS / AAA / ClearPass identity policy. Identity enforcement changes must be approved by a human — an agent can log the recommendation but cannot commit.

enforcement.guarantee: Blocks the matching action only on hook, MCP, and runtime surfaces when their listed dependencies are satisfied. Does NOT inspect LLM prompt or response text.
requires: A supported pre-tool hook is installed, synced, and invoked before the action
The agent invokes MCP guard_check with accurate tool_name and tool_input before acting
Conduct workflow runtime Guard is enabled and matching content is present in workflow state
known_limitations: Regex is verb-based; new ClearPass API paths or vendor CLI dialects require pattern updates
Does not intercept identity changes made via GUI sessions the agent does not shell out

rules.description: Block agent shell actions that install, load, or activate a network device firmware / OS image (Junos, ArubaOS, ArubaOS-CX, Aruba Instant). Firmware changes — especially downgrades — must be approved by a human because they can silently reintroduce known CVEs and reset feature flags.
rules.message: Blocked: this action would change network device firmware. Firmware updates and especially downgrades require human approval — an autonomous agent should propose the version and change window, not commit it.

enforcement.guarantee: Blocks the matching action only on hook, MCP, and runtime surfaces when their listed dependencies are satisfied. Does NOT inspect LLM prompt or response text.
requires: A supported pre-tool hook is installed, synced, and invoked before the action
The agent invokes MCP guard_check with accurate tool_name and tool_input before acting
Conduct workflow runtime Guard is enabled and matching content is present in workflow state
known_limitations: Cannot distinguish upgrade from downgrade without inspecting the target version — treats all image changes as approval-required
Vendor out-of-band firmware paths (Aruba Central push, ZTP boot) that bypass device shell are not intercepted

rules.description: Block agent shell actions that reassign VLAN membership across many ports at once — interface ranges, port-access role rebinds, or scripted loops. Single-port moves stay allowed; broadcast-scope changes require human approval to prevent an agent from splitting a floor or a data center off the network.
rules.message: Blocked: this action would reassign VLAN membership across multiple ports at once. Broadcast-scope VLAN moves must be approved by a human — agents can propose the plan and per-port sequence but cannot commit the bulk change.

Cannot detect a bulk change delivered as many separate CLI sessions from a controller
